source.title: A Factor Graph Description of Deep Temporal Active Inference

confidence_rationale: Direction convention: 'weakens' = weakens the distinct-novel-object reading. This paper puts active inference -- directed generative model, variational message passing, AND policy/action selection by expected-free-energy minimisation -- ON a Forney-style factor graph. That places capacities (a) directed update, (b) cyclic/undirected coherence (factor-graph substrate), AND action coupling under ONE object and ONE inference algorithm. It is the bridge entry showing the DLIF 'action loop' is not extra to the graphical-model substrate. Held at 0.72 because it does not itself demonstrate (c) structure learning or (d) scale -- those are the companion entries (Smith 2020, RGM 2024).
failure_signatures: The factor-graph active-inference formulation assumes a specified generative model structure; latent-node birth/death (capacity c) requires the separate structure-learning machinery (Smith 2020 / Bayesian model reduction).
Scale/granularity (capacity d) is present only as fixed hierarchical depth here, not as a renormalisation operator (that is the RGM 2024 contribution).

mapping.source_claim_statement: Active inference -- perception, learning, and policy selection -- can be specified entirely as message passing (free-energy minimisation) on a Forney-style factor graph representing a deep temporal generative model.
mapping.ree_translation: DLIF's 'action coupling' capacity, which the research map attributes to active inference as a separate formalism from the graphical-model substrate, is in fact realised ON the factor graph itself. (a) directed update + (b) cyclic coherence + action selection are one object, not three to be unified.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Covers (a)+(b)+action coupling + precision (precision = inverse variance is intrinsic to AI). Does not deliver (c) or (d) by itself, and contains no residue/non-erasure primitive. Weakens, does not fully collapse, the DLIF novelty claim.
mapping.source_context: Tutorial / methodological paper in computational neuroscience; synthetic agent, no clinical or moral content.

confidence_components.notes: Authored by Friston (active inference's originator) + de Vries (ForneyLab). High fidelity to the 'one substrate carries inference + action' claim. Transfer risk moderate: REE's selection/commitment machinery is not literally EFE-minimisation, so 'action coupling exists in AI' transfers as an existence proof, not as REE's exact mechanism.
